methodology: Unweighted simple average of the candidate’s share in each opened national 2028 GOP primary poll that reported that candidate (7 polls). These polls use different universes (open-ended intended primary voters; likely Republican primary voters; GOP side of a midterm-voter survey; likely voters; self-selected GOP-primary RVs; Emerson closed-ended list of GOP-primary RVs; Verasight list question among Republican adults) and are not strictly comparable. A RealClearPolitics 2028 nomination page was blocked (403) and was not used. Aggregator tables that were not opened as primary sources were not used, except that the Echelon Insights result was read from a Polling Desk poll page that cites the NYT/PollResults feed. Nov 20, 2026: no new national 2028 GOP primary polls were found since the Emerson release (Nov 19). Posts on X reported that the RealClearPolitics 2028 average now shows Rubio 35.4% and Vance 34.0%; the RCP page again returned 403, so that figure is not used here. Nov 21, 2026: added the Strength In Numbers/Verasight poll (Nov 11–13; released Nov 19), which had been missed. Average moved from Vance 35.0 / Rubio 31.3 / DeSantis 12.3 (6 polls) to Vance 33.9 / Rubio 31.6 / DeSantis 13.3 (7 polls). A First Tuesday Strategies South Carolina poll (Nov 19, 2,062 RV: Rubio 38.5, Vance 16.8, DeSantis 13.4, as relayed on X) is a single-state poll and is not part of this national average. The RCP 2028 page again returned 403 and was not used. Nov 22, 2026: no new national 2028 GOP primary polls; the RealClearPolling latest-polls page (opened this time) still lists Emerson (Nov 19) as the newest. Online straw polls relayed on X (StrawPoll.us: Rubio 48.2, Vance 19.7; the “People’s Poll”: Rubio 57, Vance 7) are self-selected and not used. Averages unchanged.

polls.sample: 418 Republican primary voters within a national survey of 1,000 registered voters
polls.universe: Registered voters planning to vote in the GOP primary (closed-ended list)
polls.moe: ±3 points on the 1,000 voters; subsample MoE not stated.
polls.note: Released Nov 19, 2026. The closed-ended list question (44 / 24 / 9) is used in the average because the other polls here mostly read from candidate lists; the open-ended question had Rubio 36, Vance 20, DeSantis 7, Trump 7, Massie 7. USA Today notes the same pollster had Vance ahead of Rubio 54%–6% a year earlier. Subsample size (418) from USA Today.

polls.sample: 632 Republicans (listed as 632 A by PollResults) within a national survey of about 1,400 adults from both parties
polls.moe: ±2.6 points on the full survey (Political Wire); about ±3.9 on the 632-person GOP sample (Polling Desk).
polls.note: Released Nov 19, 2026 (missed in the Nov 20 update). The poll asked an open text-box question and then a candidate-list question. The 33 / 27 / 19 figures (Don't know 8, None 5) are reported by Political Wire, PollResults and the New York Daily News and are used in the average, consistent with using closed-ended list questions elsewhere. Polling Desk (NYT/PollResults feed) lists 26 / 19 / 9 for the same field dates and sample; which question that reflects was not confirmed on a page opened, so it is shown separately and not averaged. G. Elliott Morris: 'Rubio’s lead comes almost entirely from the hawks'; Vance leads among Republicans who want to end the Iran war and among white blue-collar workers. Verasight’s previous reading (ended Apr 23) had Vance +21, per Polling Desk.

polls.moe: About ±4.9 points (per the Polling Desk page).
polls.note: Published Nov 17, 2026. Echelon's previous poll (ended Oct 19) had Vance +18 over Rubio; this one is Vance +14. Read from the Polling Desk poll page (data feed: The New York Times via PollResults.org); the Echelon release itself was not opened.

polls.sample: Republican-primary voters within an online survey of 920 registered voters (39% chose the GOP primary); subsample size not stated.
polls.universe: Self-selected GOP primary voters (all RVs asked which primary)
polls.moe: ±4.2 points on the 920 RVs; larger for the primary sample (not stated).
polls.note: Online via Cint, weighted with an MRP frame. Without Vance: Rubio 42, DeSantis 18, Cruz 8, Carlson 7. Same poll: Ossoff and Newsom each lead Vance by 13 in general-election matchups. A newer, small pollster whose questions were crowdsourced from X followers; treat with caution.

polls.sample: Intended 2028 Republican primary voters, within a survey of 1,685 U.S. adult citizens. GOP subsample size was not stated on the article page.
polls.moe: Parent poll ~±3 percentage points (1,685 adults); subsample MoE not stated.
polls.note: Open-ended question, AI-coded. Also reports MAGA split: Vance 45 / Rubio 35 / DeSantis 10; non-MAGA: Vance 33 / Rubio 29 / DeSantis 19.

polls.sample: Likely Republican primary voters, from a survey of 1,090 U.S. likely voters conducted Nov 5 and 8–9, 2026. GOP subsample size was not stated on the public (non-paywalled) page.
polls.moe: ±3 percentage points on the 1,090 likely-voter survey; subsample MoE not stated on the public page.
polls.note: Public write-up compares to July: Vance down from 39%; Rubio unchanged; DeSantis up from 7%. Other candidates were not listed on the public portion of the page. Field work by Pulse Opinion Research, LLC.

polls.sample: 3,000 midterm voters (National Voter Trends post-mortem). GOP 2028 subsample size was not stated.
polls.note: Cygnal says “on the GOP side” Rubio leads Vance 34–31, with DeSantis third at 14%. Traditional Republicans prefer Rubio 36% to Vance 30%. Other candidates were not listed in this write-up.
